Title: Corporate earnings pick up, but misses still outnumber beats: CIMB Securities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's second quarter (Q2) of 2026 corporate earnings season has shown a modest improvement from the previous quarter, although the beat-to-miss ratio remains below last year's level, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd.
In a note, the firm said 56 companies, or 56 per cent of its coverage, had reported their Q2 results as of Aug 23.
Of these, 14 per cent, or eight companies, beat expectations, while 23 per cent, or 13 companies, missed estimates. The remaining 63 per cent, or 35 companies, met expectations.
CIMB Securities said the beat-to-miss ratio improved to 0.62 times from 0.52 times in the first quarter of 2026, but remained below the 0.88 times recorded in Q2 of 2025.
Year-on-year earnings growth was led by Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd, Westports Holdings Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd, Top Glove Corp Bhd and Genting Plantations Bhd.
The growth was driven by higher average selling prices, tariff increases, gains from industrial land sales and stronger fresh fruit bunches output.
Among the 26 FBM KLCI constituents covered by CIMB Securities, 12 had reported their results, with all meeting expectations except Petronas Chemicals and YTL Power International Bhd, which posted weaker-than-expected earnings.
The eight companies that beat expectations were spread across eight sectors, including oil and gas, automotive, consumer, gaming, gloves, technology, plantation and transport.
CIMB Securities said the beats were mainly driven by stronger-than-expected sales volumes or average selling prices, as well as higher contributions from associates.
In contrast, earnings misses were concentrated in the oil and gas, utilities, property and consumer sectors.
The firm also said consumer-sector misses, involving Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd (F&N), MyNews Holdings Bhd and 7-Eleven Malaysia Holdings Bhd, were largely due to weaker sales and higher operating expenses.
Oil and gas companies, including Yinson Holdings Bhd, Petronas Chemicals and Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd, were affected by weaker-than-expected sales.
Utilities players Malakoff Corp Bhd and YTL Power were weighed down by lower contributions from power plants.
Following the results, CIMB Securities upgraded Genting Plantations, Bermaz Auto Bhd, YTL Power, IGB Real Estate Investment Trust and Sunway Real Estate Investment Trust to "Buy" from "Hold".
It also raised VS Industry Bhd to "Hold" from "Sell".
Meanwhile, AMMB Holdings Bhd, Affin Bank Bhd and MyNews were downgraded to "Hold" from "Buy", while Top Glove was cut to "Reduce" from "Hold".
CIMB Securities maintained its FBM KLCI target at 1,745 points and recommended Genting Plantations, YTL Power, IGB REIT, Sunway REIT and Bermaz Auto, citing improved risk-reward profiles following their Q2 results.
The firm said the earnings season's beat-to-miss ratio was tracking higher quarter-on-quarter but lower year-on-year, while earnings growth continued to be supported by stronger contributions from Petronas Chemicals, Westports, SD Guthrie, glove makers and technology companies.

Title: Dutch say won't participate in 'no longer' neutral Eurovision
Article:
THE HAGUE: The Netherlands will not participate in next year's Eurovision Song Contest, its broadcaster said Monday, saying the event can "no longer be considered neutral" given divisions over the Gaza war.
"It is undeniable that international conflicts are increasingly affecting the Contest, undermining its neutral character.
The Eurovision Song Contest has therefore become a platform for division," said Taco Zimmerman, Director-General of AVROTROS in a statement from the broadcaster.
The contest has recently been hit by a wave of boycotts over Israel's participation.
Earlier this month, organisers announced they were excluding any country involved in an armed conflict from hosting the competition.
"However, the recently announced changes... do not provide sufficient confidence that the independent and neutral character of the Eurovision Song Contest has been restored," said the AVROTROS statement.
Israel came close to winning the competition in both 2025 and 2026, ultimately finishing second on each occasion.
Next year's event, the world's biggest live televised music event, will take place on May 15 in Bulgaria's Black Sea city of Burgas.
It will be the first time that the Balkan nation hosts the contest, coming after Bulgarian singer Darina Yotova, known as Dara, won this year's contest in the Austrian capital Vienna with the catchy floor-filler "Bangaranga."
Since its launch in 1955, Eurovision has become the ultimate pop platform, catapulting Swedish icons ABBA to worldwide fame, as well as boosting the likes of Celine Dion, Cliff Richard and Olivia Newton-John.
The 2026 competition was watched by 131 million viewers, down 35 million on the year before after five countries boycotted it over Israel's participation.
The Netherlands, Iceland, Spain, Ireland and Slovenia all pulled out of the contest – with the latter three refusing to broadcast the show at all.

Title: Police tighten border security, urge public to avoid southern Thailand
Article:
MELAKA: Police have stepped up security along the Malaysia-Thailand border following more than 50 bombings, arson attacks on government offices and tyre-burning incidents reported in three southern Thai provinces last Saturday.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail also urged Malaysians to avoid travelling to conflict zones in southern Thailand amid the heightened tensions.
"We are increasing border controls because we are concerned, first and foremost, about Malaysians who frequently visit the area.
"In my view, given the current tense security situation, our people should reduce travel there and avoid visiting conflict zones for now. That is the best course of action," he said.
He told reporters this after the awards, decorations and medals ceremony held in conjunction with the 77th birthday of Yang Dipertua Negeri Melaka Tun Mohd Ali Rustam at Seri Negeri, Ayer Keroh, today.
Earlier, Khalid received the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (D.G.S.M.), which carries the title Datuk Seri.
He expressed hope the conflict would be resolved peacefully to ensure continued security along the border.
"We pray that everything can be settled amicably, and that both countries, especially along the border, remain safe and peaceful," he said.
Meanwhile, a curfew was imposed in Narathiwat from 10.15pm on Aug 22 until 5am the following day following more than 50 violent incidents reported across three provinces.
The explosions, heard from Narathiwat, sent shockwaves through border communities, rattling homes and alarming residents in Kampung Lubok Gong and Kampung Tersang in Rantau Panjang.

Title: Haze worsens as 16 areas record unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings nationwide rose to 16 from 10 recorded earlier this morning.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), as of 4pm today, Sarawak was the worst-hit state, with Serian recording the country's highest API reading at 192, nearing the "very unhealthy" threshold.
Other areas in Sarawak that logged unhealthy air quality included Kuching (181), Samarahan (173), Sri Aman (156), Bintulu (145), and Mukah (134).
In Peninsular Malaysia, Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest reading at 162.
Two stations in Kedah also registered high unhealthy levels, with Sungai Petani at 155 and Alor Star at 151.
Perak also saw elevated readings in Seri Manjung (134) and Tasek Ipoh (115), while Minden in Penang registered an API of 117.
Other areas in the Klang Valley recording unhealthy air included Kuala Selangor (112) and Shah Alam (105).
Putrajaya recorded a reading of 102, while Cheras in Kuala Lumpur hovered just above the threshold at 101.
An API reading between 0 and 50 is categorised as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and 300 and above as hazardous.
Earlier today, Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the haze affecting several parts of the country was unlikely to clear until open burning in neighbouring countries was brought under control.
He said
the current hot and dry spell
, which is expected to dominate the weather pattern over the next few days, had exacerbated the situation.
Prevailing winds from Kalimantan and Sumatra were carrying transboundary haze directly into Sarawak and the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia.
Meanwhile, nearly 20 other stations nationwide recorded API readings at the upper end of the "moderate" category, nearing the unhealthy threshold.
Three stations recorded an API of 99 — just two points shy of the unhealthy threshold — namely Tanjung Malim in Perak, Bukit Rambai in Melaka, and Kota Tinggi in Johor.
In Penang, three stations also approached the unhealthy mark: Seberang Perai (98), Seberang Jaya (97), and Balik Pulau (97), alongside Taiping in Perak (97).
Other areas recording high moderate readings included Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur (96); Nilai, Seremban, and Segamat (95 each); Pegoh Ipoh (94); Kangar and Klang (93 each); Banting, Batu Pahat, and Samalaju in Sarawak (92 each); as well as Kulim Hi-Tech and Kluang (91 each).

Title: Trump's Kim gambit deepens doubts over US reliability at key moment for Asia
Article:
DONALD Trump's olive branch to North Korea's Kim Jong Un at the expense of a long-standing ally comes at a pivotal moment for US security ties in Asia, as partners from Japan to India reassess how much they can rely on Washington.
The US president's abrupt decision to cut back military drills with South Korea last week, which he described as hostile to Pyongyang, has reinforced fears that Trump's unpredictability could strain alliances that have long maintained peace in the region, government officials and security experts said.
Japan worries it too could find itself in Trump's cross-hairs as it embarks on thorny security negotiations; Taiwan is warily watching an upcoming summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping; and India is growing less certain of its place in Washington's strategic calculus.
"The decision will certainly fuel growing doubts in the region about US security commitments," said Jeremy Chan, a senior analyst with political risk consultancy Eurasia Group and former US diplomat in Japan and China.
Adding to the anxiety, the United States cancelled another military exercise with South Korea scheduled for next month, Seoul said on Monday, after Washington cited constraints on US forces due to the Iran war.
Trump has been frustrated by the failure of US allies to support the war and made it clear that many of them must spend more on their own defence, a White House official said when asked about such concerns.
[[nid:1517867]]
He is eager to restart talks with North Korea and secure a win on the international stage to counter his unpopular conflict with Iran, according to a person briefed on discussions between US and South Korean officials.
Trump's push to meet Kim - which has so far drawn a frosty response from Pyongyang - could backfire and embolden nuclear-armed North Korea, said Itsunori Onodera, an influential Japanese lawmaker and former defence minister.
Such a prospect is "extremely troubling" for Tokyo, he said on a Fuji TV news programme last Thursday.
Despite Trump's overtures, Pyongyang fired a volley of ballistic missiles off its east coast earlier that day, triggering alerts in neighbouring South Korea and Japan.
What worries Japanese officials more is Trump's approach as Tokyo embarks on talks with Washington over how much it should pay towards the cost of hosting US forces, America's largest overseas deployment.
Japan is bracing for the possibility that Trump could, with little warning, demand a sharp hike that would be politically difficult to swallow, said a senior Japanese government official, requesting anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter.
Trump could also wield upcoming US military exercises with Japan in October as leverage, analysts say.
Officials in Washington and Tokyo said they did not expect the exercises to be curtailed, though Trump could change his mind at any point, they cautioned.
[[nid:1517866]]
The drills, known as Keen Sword, may already be smaller than their 2024 iteration because of the diversion of US assets and personnel to the conflict with Iran.
That shift - which recently saw America's only forward-deployed aircraft carrier in Asia, the USS George Washington, depart for the Middle East to relieve the beleaguered USS Abraham Lincoln - has stirred concern that US deterrence against China is being eroded.
During a visit to Asia this month, Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby said working with allies to ensure combat readiness along the so-called first island chain that runs from Japan through the Philippines is a priority for Washington.
Nowhere are concerns about China's growing military pressure more acute than in Taiwan, the democratically governed island claimed by Beijing.
Trump has held up approval of a US$14 billion package of arms sales to Taipei in order to maintain warm relations and a fragile trade truce with China's Xi.
As Trump prepares for his latest round of summitry with Xi in Washington next month, officials in Taipei say they expect Washington will at the very least carve up the arms sales into smaller chunks to try and avoid upsetting Beijing too much.
Domingo Yang of the Taiwan defence ministry's think tank, the Institute for National Defence and Security Research, says there is a distinction between Trump's rhetoric and actual US behaviour, noting US intelligence sharing, training and patrols with Taiwan remain substantial.
[[nid:1517865]]
A US Navy aircraft transited the Taiwan Strait on Friday in a move the United States described as demonstrating its "commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific."
Trump's latest actions have also rocked confidence in India, where the US risks squandering years of efforts to draw New Delhi closer as a counterweight to Russia and China, security analysts say.
It also comes after the Pentagon's decision in June to rename its Asia military headquarters to Pacific Command from Indo-Pacific Command, a move some analysts say is a sign India is no longer as strategically important to Washington.
The Pentagon denied any such shift. But Trump's steep tariffs on Indian exports and repeated claims that he had mediated an India-Pakistan ceasefire had already exasperated New Delhi.
Officials there are now "very, very cautious" about committing to long-term defence deals with Washington, according to two Indian sources with knowledge of the matter.
"The latest decision only reinforces President Trump's transactional view of foreign affairs and serves as a reminder that differences over specific policies, even among allies, can carry costs for the broader bilateral relationship," said Pearl Pandya, senior analyst at Armed Conflict Location & Event Data, a conflict monitoring group.
* The writers are from Reuters

Title: Finas to investigate allegations of cartel in film industry
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) will summon exhibitors, distributors and film producers to investigate allegations of a cartel and market dominance in the local film industry.
Its chief executive officer, Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib, said that although no official complaints had been received so far, Finas was taking proactive steps to gather information and understand the situation in the industry.
"Officially, Finas has not received any complaints, but that does not mean we are not paying attention and we are currently gathering information.
"We will call all parties, including cinemas (exhibitors), distributors and producers, to discuss and understand the current landscape," he told reporters after the Engagement Session with the Finas Chief Executive Officer: National Film Policy 2026-2035 at the Finas Tower in Damansara here today.
Azmir said the main concern was not merely about a single distributor dominating the entire market, but rather the possibility of an entity being involved at several levels of the industry chain as a distributor, publisher and cinema owner.
He said the review had so far found that no company possessed all three licences simultaneously, in accordance with the Finas Act, which limits a company to holding a maximum of two categories of licences.
However, Azmir said the investigation would also cover the possibility that cross-chain operations were carried out through subsidiaries or different business entities.
Meanwhile, he said Finas had received a notification from a local Tamil film producer regarding the last-minute entry of a film from India, which allegedly disrupted the producer's film screening schedule.
To address the issue, Azmir said Finas was examining mechanisms to require advance notification for the entry of international films, similar to the approach in Singapore, which mandates notification at least a month before screening.
Azmir said schedule coordination was important to protect domestic films in all languages, including Malay, Tamil and Chinese, from facing competition with foreign films targeting the same audience. -- BERNAMA

Title: 57 held in Seremban raids on budget hotels linked to prostitution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers arrested 57 people in raids on three locations in Seremban believed to have been used for prostitution activities involving foreign women.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation was carried out from 2pm yesterday by officers from the Intelligence and Special Operations Division at Immigration headquarters in Putrajaya, with the cooperation of the Indonesian Embassy in Kuala Lumpur.
He said the raids followed information from the embassy concerning Indonesians allegedly involved in immoral activities, followed by intelligence gathering by the department.

Title: Khazanah deploys RM15bil under GEAR-uP initiative – Amirul Feisal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah Nasional Bhd has deployed RM15 billion to date of its RM25 billion five-year domestic investment commitment under the Finance Ministry's GEAR-uP initiative.
Khazanah Nasional's managing director Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir said the sovereign wealth fund's deployment forms part of the broader RM120 billion domestic direct investment (DDI) target by government-linked investment companies (GLICs) for the period from 2024 to 2028.
"Of that RM120 billion, Khazanah has committed RM25 billion, and we have deployed about RM15 billion to date. That is our track record," he said during Bernama TV's The Nation programme titled: Backing Malaysia's Next Generation of Growth.
The GEAR-uP programme, involving Khazanah, the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP), Lembaga Tabung Angkatan Tentera (LTAT) and Lembaga Tabung Haji, recorded a sharp increase in domestic investments of RM20.3 billion in 2025, a threefold increase from the RM6.6 billion DDI deployed in 2024.
Khazanah contributed the largest share at RM7.9 billion, followed by the EPF with RM5.8 billion, KWAP with RM5.4 billion and PNB with RM1.3 billion.
He pointed out that the drive for increased domestic investments aligns with a global trend, which is also evident in major economies such as the United States, Europe, Canada, and Australia.
This trend has emerged in response to disruptions in global trade and supply chains caused by geopolitical tensions and tariffs.
Amirul Feisal said Khazanah's role under the initiative is to catalyse innovation and support mid-tier companies with growth potential, helping them scale up and eventually access capital markets.
"It is almost like a relay race. We support companies at the growth stage, and eventually they can transition into mature sectors, where larger GLICs can step in, including through avenues such as initial public offerings (IPO).
"So far, we see good traction; we have invested significantly into the Dana Impak, energy transition clusters, and we are seeing traction in the growth there," he said.
On balancing national development objectives with investment returns, Amirul Feisal said Khazanah adopts a cluster-based approach to align commercial viability with strategic priorities.
"For example, we have grouped assets such as airports, airlines and tourism under aviation connectivity. The goal is to improve connectivity for trade, tourism and business, which then creates a multiplier effect across related sectors such as maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO).
"Similarly, investments in energy transition are driven by both national priorities and commercial considerations. We want to accelerate the shift to renewable energy to enhance resilience against global energy shocks.
At the same time, these are still commercial investments, but it is also a national priority," he said.

Title: 120 vehicles set for 630km Pahang expedition
Article:
A total of 120 vehicles will take part in Malayan Xpedition (MX) 2026, traversing a 630-kilometre (km) route that spans highways and challenging, unpaved logging tracks deep in the interior of Pahang.
The six-day, five-night expedition is fully booked, with the organiser setting technical, safety and route-management standards to ensure the cross-country journey is conducted safely and responsibly.
Organised by By The Billions (BTB), the expedition combines exploration, vehicle capability and environmental responsibility throughout the convoy.
In line with the approach, BTB has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Enggang Management Services (EMS) and the Al-Sultan Abdullah Royal Tiger Reserve (ASARTR), integrating conservation efforts into the convoy's logistics through a Habitat Enrichment Project.
To ensure operational safety and minimise disruption along the 630km route, all participating vehicles and field operations will be subject to mandatory technical inspections.
MX 2026 is supported by a line-up of sponsors and technical partners.
This is led by title sponsor GWM and official lubricant partner Grantt Lubricants, alongside BFGoodrich, Alpaka Gear, Victron Energy, Pedders Malaysia, Red Springs Overland, Tough Dog Suspension Malaysia and ANBOT.
The technical partnerships cover equipment required to handle heavy loads and vehicle recovery situations along Pahang's challenging unpaved logging tracks.
[[nid:1517854]]
A fleet of sweeper, medical and mobile recovery vehicles will also be deployed to maintain convoy safety.
Before the official departure, all participating vehicles must undergo technical inspections during the public Adventure Festival, formerly known as 4Wheels Fest, on Sept 12 at PARC, Subang Jaya.
BTB founder Nedree Mohd Nazlan said vehicle capability must go hand in hand with driver discipline and environmental responsibility in off-road activities.
"Off-road activities are a combination of vehicle preparation, driver discipline and environmental responsibility," he said.
From a technical perspective, the mandatory inspections will cover chassis recovery points, winches, braking systems and waterproof electrical systems to ensure the vehicles are prepared for remote routes through forested corridors.
All-terrain and mud-terrain tyres are also recommended, supported by industry partners.
This includes BFGoodrich, Pedders Malaysia and Tough Dog Suspension Malaysia to meet the demands of carrying heavy loads on challenging logging tracks.
At the same time, the convoy team will collect, transport and plant 500 fig tree (Ficus sp.) saplings from the ASARTR Central Nursery in Kampung Mat Daling, Pahang, to help strengthen the food supply for the endangered Malayan tiger.
BTB will also carry out a 12-month monitoring and maintenance programme, tracking the growth of the saplings and replacing those that do not survive before submitting a complete record to ASARTR.
To prevent environmental degradation and habitat fragmentation, the convoy will use existing logging roads permitted by the Jerantut District Forestry Department.
Route-sweeper vehicles equipped with satellite communications, medical equipment and heavy-duty recovery gear will also be deployed to maintain convoy integrity from Selangor to Cherating.

Title: Malaysia tightens Thai border security after southern attacks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have stepped up security preparedness along the Malaysia-Thailand border following a series of explosions and attacks in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, with the situation remaining under control.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the measures included deploying personnel from the Southeast and Northern Brigades of the General Operations Force (GOF), as well as intensifying patrols along the border fencing, Sungai Golok and routes that could potentially be used for infiltration.
"JKDNKA gives assurances that the country's borders remain under control," he said when contacted here today.
He said the police was also strengthening prevention, early detection and rapid response measures, while increasing intelligence and information sharing with Thai security agencies.
Yusri said there had been no reports of Malaysians being affected by the incidents so far.
He said the Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok and Malaysian Consulate General in Songkhla would continue to liaise with Thai authorities for the latest developments and ensure the safety of Malaysians in the affected areas.
Yusri also advised Malaysians residing in, travelling to or planning to travel to southern Thailand to postpone non-essential trips and remain vigilant.
He said they should comply with all security instructions issued by Thai authorities, including any curfew imposed, as well as register and update their information via the e-Konsular portal to facilitate consular assistance in emergencies.
The media previously reported that Narathiwat was placed under a curfew from 10.15pm last Saturday to 5am yesterday following more than 50 incidents, including bombings, the burning of local government offices and tyres, reported across the three provinces.
Explosions from the direction of Narathiwat also shook homes and caused concern among residents in the Malaysia-Thailand border area, including Kampung Lubok Gong and Kampung Tersang in Rantau Panjang.

Title: Iran warns vessels violating Hormuz transit rules of fines, detention
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran has issued a warning that vessels violating its arrangements for transiting the Strait of Hormuz could face restrictions, including fines, detention, or confiscation, the Persian Gulf Strait Authority wrote in a post on X.
The warning heightens risks for the charterers and ship owners whose vessels transit through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the world's energy shipments.
The PGSA, a new body Iran has established with the aim of managing the strait, has said cargo owners should refer to an updated list of vessels deemed non-compliant for voyages relating to the Persian Gulf.
Vessels engaging in operations including ship-to-ship transfers or transshipment with non-compliant vessels will also be added to the restricted list, it said.
Ships seeking the removal of their names from the non-compliant vessels' list must submit a request with relevant explanations to Iran's maritime authorities, the post said.

Title: Southeast Asia's budget airlines eye recovery but fuel scars linger
Article:
HONG KONG: Southeast Asia's budget carriers are hoping the worst of the Middle East-driven fuel shock is behind them but face a difficult second half as margins remain under pressure and strained household budgets threaten demand, airline executives and analysts said.
The latest quarterly results from Malaysia's AirAsia, Singapore Airlines' budget arm Scoot and the Philippines' Cebu Pacific showed that efforts to recoup soaring fuel costs through higher fares fell short. AirAsia and Cebu Pacific reported net losses, while Scoot's operating loss nearly doubled.
The results exposed a squeeze at the heart of the low-cost model: fuel makes up a larger share of expenses than at full-service airlines, but price-sensitive passengers leave carriers less scope to lift fares without weakening demand.
Currency declines added to the pressure as the Malaysian ringgit, Thai baht, Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso weakened against the dollar, increasing fuel and aircraft leasing costs typically priced in US currency.
"The second quarter was the most challenging operating environment Cebu Pacific has faced post-pandemic," CEO Mike Szucs said on an earnings call this month.
The airline's fuel expense more than doubled from a year earlier, another executive said, with the impact magnified by an 8 per cent weakening of the peso. Cebu Pacific has hedged about 30 per cent of its third-quarter fuel needs at below US$120 per barrel to secure near-term protection.
Full-service airlines have been better protected by strong post-pandemic demand from premium passengers, said Nathan Gee, head of Asia-Pacific transportation research at BofA Global Research. Budget carriers have benefited less because of their more basic products and smaller loyalty programmes, he said.
BETTING ON A FOURTH-QUARTER RECOVERY
AirAsia is bracing for a weak third quarter, which it says is typically the softest for regional travel. The airline plans to cut seat capacity by 20 per cent to 25 per cent year-on-year in the quarter, return 25 older aircraft to lessors during 2026 and suspend its Sydney-Kuala Lumpur route from October as part of a broader network recalibration.
CEO Bo Lingam said in a statement that the airline was taking a "deliberate, tactical approach" to protect its bottom line after average jet fuel prices reached US$183 a barrel in the second quarter. AirAsia also recorded a net foreign exchange loss of about US$82 million.
Lingam said the airline expects to restore capacity to pre-war levels in the fourth quarter, with forward bookings tracking in line with last year.
Scoot has continued to add capacity as demand remains strong. But its passenger unit costs rose 21.7 per cent in the three months to June, pushing its operating loss to S$32 million (US$25.2 million) from S$17 million a year earlier despite higher fares and coverage under parent Singapore Airlines' fuel-hedging programme.
The cost increase lifted Scoot's break-even load factor to 100 per cent, meaning it would have needed to fill every seat to cover its passenger operating costs, against an actual load factor of 90.6 per cent.
Scoot Chief Commercial Officer Calvin Chan said in a statement to Reuters that the carrier's fare adjustments had not fully offset higher fuel prices, while the Middle East conflict continued to cloud the outlook.
A decline in fuel prices would ease immediate cost pressures but could encourage airlines to restore capacity and compete more aggressively on fares, Gee said.
Intra-Asian routes were particularly exposed because supplies of narrowbody aircraft were recovering faster than those of widebody jets, he said. That additional capacity could run up against weaker demand.
Independent aviation analyst Brendan Sobie said strained household budgets could curb travel by Southeast Asia's middle class during the rest of the year and the crucial peak season.
"The short-term outlook is rather bleak," he said. "While there is hope of improvement in the fourth quarter, it is too early to really gauge."

Title: Mara takes first step towards setting up its own hospital
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Majlis Amanah Rakyat (Mara) has taken the first steps towards establishing its first hospital by forming a special task force to drive the initiative, says its chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
He said Mara already had a comprehensive healthcare ecosystem to support the hospital, including 160 U.n.i KLINIK, U.n.i Farmasi and U.n.i Dental outlets, as well as institutions producing medical and healthcare professionals.
"The special task force to drive the establishment of Hospital Mara has been formed.
"Mara has a complete ecosystem for a hospital, with 160 U.n.i KLINIK, U.n.i Farmasi and U.n.i Dental outlets, UniKL Royal College of Medicine Perak (RCMP) producing doctors and Kolej Poly-Tech Mara (KPTM) training nurses," he said in a Facebook post today.
Asyraf said the time had come for Mara to establish its own hospital, which would serve as a teaching hospital, centre of healthcare excellence and catalyst for Bumiputera economic development.
He said the hospital would complete Mara's education ecosystem, particularly that of Universiti Kuala Lumpur Royal College of Medicine Perak (UniKL RCMP), which offers healthcare programmes including nursing, pharmacy and physiotherapy.
Clinical training and experience at a teaching hospital were essential to completing the education ecosystem, he said.
Mara also has supporting capabilities in technical and vocational education and training (TVET), engineering and technology, entrepreneurship, financing and industry development.
He said biomedical science programmes at UniKL Malaysian Institute of Medical Science Technology (UniKL MESTECH) and technology disciplines at other UniKL campuses could also be integrated into the Hospital Mara ecosystem.
"Hospital Mara could even serve as a living laboratory for Mara students and researchers. KPTM students could be involved in hospital equipment and systems technology, UniKL RCMP students could undergo clinical training, while other UniKL campuses could develop AI, IoT, robotics or medical devices.
"Mara entrepreneurs could also supply products and services to the ecosystem," he said.
Asyraf said the U.n.i KLINIK, U.n.i Farmasi and U.n.i Dental network, operated by Bumiputera professional entrepreneurs under the Professional Entrepreneur Development (ProSPEC) programme, could serve as a frontline healthcare network supporting the hospital.
"After decades of producing doctors, nurses, pharmacists and healthcare professionals, the time has come for Mara not only to produce professionals for the healthcare industry, but also to build and own an institution where they can serve, conduct research and ultimately lead the industry," he said.

Title: Bank Negara approved MNRB's acquisition of Labuan Re
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MNRB Holdings Bhd has secured Bank Negara Malaysia's approval to acquire an 80 per cent stake in Labuan Reinsurance (L) Ltd (Labuan Re) for US$100.69 million (RM400.49 million), bringing the proposed deal closer to completion.
In a bourse filing, MNRB said the central bank approved the acquisition on Aug 21 under Section 85(1)(a) of the Financial Services Act 2013, subject to the company obtaining the necessary regulatory approval from the Labuan Financial Services Authority (Labuan FSA).
The approval is one of several conditions attached to the proposed acquisition, which was first announced on May 19.
MNRB had entered into a conditional share purchase agreement to acquire 120 million shares, representing the remaining 80 per cent equity interest in Labuan Re, from 10 existing shareholders for the cash consideration.
Upon completion, MNRB will hold 80 per cent of Labuan Re directly, while its unit Malaysian Reinsurance Bhd (Malaysian Re) will retain its existing 20 per cent stake, making Labuan Re a wholly-owned subsidiary of MNRB.
MNRB said in its initial announcement that the transaction is expected to strengthen its regional and international reinsurance platform, with Labuan Re providing access to multiple markets through its general reinsurance and retakaful businesses.
Labuan Re also participates in the Lloyd's market through its wholly-owned subsidiary Labuan Re Underwriting Ltd, giving the group access to specialised underwriting opportunities and international risk pools.
MNRB had previously said the acquisition was expected to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory and shareholder approvals.
Besides Bank Negara and Labuan FSA approvals, the deal requires approval from MNRB's non-interested shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting, regulatory approval from Lloyd's relating to the indirect change of control of Labuan Re Underwriting, and consent from RHB Bank (L) Ltd in relation to Labuan Re's subordinated bonds.
The acquisition is a related-party transaction under Bursa Malaysia's Main Market listing requirements, as MNRB and several vendors share common interests involving Permodalan Nasional Bhd.
The vendors comprise CIMB Bank Bhd, Hicom Holdings Bhd, MISC Bhd, Petroliam Nasional Bhd, Telekom Malaysia Bhd, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, Lembaga Tabung Angkatan Tentera, Malayan Banking Bhd, Public Bank Bhd and RHB Bank Bhd.
Labuan Re recorded unaudited insurance and takaful contract revenue of US$165.17 million (RM704.75million),net investment income of US$39.11 million (RM166.87 million) and net profit of US$19.4 million (RM82.78 million) for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025.

Title: Forensic analysis links 15 loose pages to Zara Qairina's journal, inquest told
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: There is strong scientific support for the conclusion that 15 loose pages examined in the inquest into Zara Qairina Mahathir's death originally came from a "Love and Peace" journal labelled WK9, the Coroner's Court heard today.
Forensic science lecturer and researcher Dr Dzulkiflee Ismail said the finding was based on chemical analysis of the 15 loose pages, marked Y1 to Y15, and the WK9 journal.
The 78th witness said he was asked to determine whether the paper used for the loose pages came from the same source as that used in WK9.
A new, unused "Love and Peace" journal of the same type was also examined as a control sample.
"Taken together, my results support the conclusion that the paper of pages Y1 to Y15 share the same chemical composition as the paper of journal WK9 and is chemically distinguishable from an unused journal of the same brand and type.
"In other words, there is strong scientific support for the conclusion that the loose pages Y1 to Y15 originally came from journal WK9," he said while reading his witness statement before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan.
Dzulkiflee said the papers underwent chemical analysis using Attenuated Total Reflectance-Fourier Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy, combined with chemometric techniques.
He said ATR-FTIR was a non-destructive technique using infrared light to produce a distinctive "fingerprint" based on the chemical composition of paper.
The analysis found that Y1 to Y15 were chemically very similar, while WK9 shared the same chemical profile as the loose pages.
In contrast, the unused journal was clearly distinct from both WK9 and Y1 to Y15.
Further statistical analysis consistently grouped WK9 with Y1 to Y15 rather than the unused control journal.
Dzulkiflee said his examination was limited to establishing the likely common origin of the paper based on its chemical composition.
He did not examine the handwriting or determine who wrote the entries, saying this was carried out separately by forensic document examiner Tay Eue Kam.
Dzulkiflee was jointly instructed with Tay and forensic science lecturer and researcher Dr Wan Nur Syuhaila Mat Desa by the legal team representing Zara's mother to examine journals, exercise books and loose sheets of paper connected with Zara for the inquest.
The original documents were examined at the Kota Kinabalu High Court over two sessions, from Sept 24 to 26 and Oct 10 and 13 to 15, 2025.
Zara, 13, was found unconscious on the ground floor of her school hostel on July 16, 2025, and was pronounced dead the following day at Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
The inquest into her death began on Sept 3, 2025.

Title: Asteel gets RM18mil takeover offer from Clifford Hii
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asteel Group Bhd says it has received an RM18 million takeover offer from businessman Clifford Hii.
Hii is seeking to take control of the steelmaker while retaining its listing status.
He entered into an agreement to buy a 53 per cent stake in Asteel from a group of substantial shareholders at 7.5 sen per share, according to an exchange filing.
The acquisition would give him a controlling interest in the company.
Under Malaysia's takeover rules, Hii is required to make a mandatory offer for the remaining shares held by Asteel's minority shareholders.
Despite seeking control of the company, Hii does not intend to privatise Asteel and plans to maintain its listing.
The takeover comes as Asteel continues to operate in an industry exposed to fluctuations in steel prices, construction activity and broader economic conditions.
The company recently announced a net profit of RM1.37 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (2Q2026), nearly four times the RM275,000 recorded a year earlier.
Revenue rose 20 per cent to RM80.67 million from RM67.3 million, driven by higher sales of coil products and increased turnover from building materials.

Title: PetDagang's Q2 earnings soar 46pct to RM387mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Dagangan Bhd's (PetDagang) net profit jumped 46 per cent to RM387 million in the second quarter of financial year 2026 (Q2 FY26) from RM265.5 million a year earlier.
This was driven by higher gross profit, particularly from its commercial segment, PetDagang said.
Its net profit rose to RM387 million from RM265.5 million a year earlier, while revenue surged 77 per cent to RM16 billion from RM9 billion previously due to higher average selling prices.
The commercial segment recorded a 70 per cent increase in revenue to RM2.92 billion, supported by an 80 per cent increase in average selling prices, which offset a six per cent decline in sales volume.
The operator of Petronas' retail fuel business declared a dividend of 25 sen per share, payable on Sept 23.
For the first half of FY26, PetDagang's net profit rose 20 per cent to RM670 million from RM559 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 50 per cent to RM27 billion from RM18 billion previously.
The company said geopolitical developments in the Middle East are expected to continue influencing global energy markets and the oil price outlook in the second half of 2026.
This will keep the global operating environment dynamic amid commodity price movements and evolving policy measures.
Despite the external headwinds, PetDagang expects Malaysia's domestic demand to remain supportive, underpinned by continued household spending, steady tourism activity and manageable inflation.
"This is further strengthened by domestic policy measures, including targeted fuel subsidies, which are expected to sustain mobility, fuel demand and retail activity.
"The group will continue to respond proactively to evolving market conditions and regulatory policies, while maintaining operational excellence and business resilience," it added.

Title: Thai man pleads not guilty to possessing 6,000 yaba pills in Kelantan
Article:
PASIR MAS: A 45-year-old Thai man pleaded not guilty at the magistrates' court here today to possessing 6,000 yaba pills in Rantau Panjang.
Saliki Deraman entered the plea after the charge was read before Magistrate Syed Farid Syed Ali.
He was alleged to have committed the offence at the roadside of Kampung Rahmat, Jalan Lubok Stol-Rantau Panjang, at 7.30pm on Aug 15.
He was charged under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, which carries the death penalty or life imprisonment, with whipping of not less than 12 strokes, upon conviction.
Saliki was also charged under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 for entering Malaysia without a travel document.
Deputy public prosecutor Nik Zharifah Insyirah Nik Zahari appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
The court set Nov 23 for mention of the case.

Title: Adults aged 31-59 make up bulk of drug abuse cases
Article:
KUALA BERANG: People aged 31 to 59 recorded the highest number of drug abuse cases in the country, with 92,590 individuals or 71.1 per cent of the total recorded from January to June this year, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (NADA) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh.
He said 34,471 people aged 15 to 30, or 26.5 per cent, were recorded during the same period, while 3,229 people aged 60 and above accounted for 2.5 per cent.
Ruslin said the statistics showed that drug abuse continued to affect various age groups, including individuals aged up to 63.
"NADA records also show that there are individuals aged up to 63 involved in drug abuse.
"For the 15 to 30 age group, 34,471 people or 26.5 per cent were recorded up to June this year, compared with 37,494 people or 27.8 per cent last year.
"The group aged below 14 recorded 17 individuals this year, compared with 14 last year," he said after the handover ceremony for the Hulu Terengganu NADA Office Renovation Project in Ajil here today.
Ruslin said drug abuse among those aged 31 to 59 and 15 to 30 primarily involved synthetic drugs, particularly in the East Coast states.
He said the number of drug abuse cases involving those aged 60 and above fell to 3,229 or 2.5 per cent this year, from 4,311 or 3.2 per cent last year.
Meanwhile, Ruslin said NADA welcomed cooperation from private companies to discuss measures to address drug abuse among employees through its Drug-Free Workplace Programme.
He said NADA, together with enforcement agencies including the police, did not differentiate between professionals and non-professionals when taking action against drug abuse, as anyone could be exposed to the problem.
One proposal to be discussed is the implementation of periodic or random urine tests as a screening measure.
"Many private companies have already implemented this programme, while some are still in the process of collaborating with NADA," he said.
Meanwhile, Ruslin said the RM3.46 million purchase and renovation project for the Hulu Terengganu district NADA office had been fully completed, providing improved facilities to strengthen operations and service delivery to the community.
He said NADA purchased four shop units in 2022 before renovation work was carried out to convert them into the district office.
"Among the facilities provided are male and female lock-ups, examination rooms, briefing rooms, consultation rooms and urine screening rooms.
"Previously, Hulu Terengganu did not have separate lock-up facilities for men and women. If there were arrests involving women, they had to be sent to another location," he said.
He said the office also functions as a Community Rehabilitation Centre, allowing clients under court orders to undergo rehabilitation programmes periodically.
"With the establishment of this office, it completes NADA's overall operations in Hulu Terengganu, enabling services to the community to be delivered more effectively," he added.

Title: E&O's Q1 net profit surges to RM58.1mil on higher revenue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Eastern & Oriental Bhd's net profit rose 27.9 per cent to RM58.11 million in the first quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM45.42 million a year ago, driven by higher revenue.
The property developer's quarterly revenue climbed 53.4 per cent to RM281.47 million from RM183.51 million previously.
This increase was mainly attributed to the properties segment, which registered RM99.3 million more.
Earnings per share rose to 2.33 sen from 1.82 sen in Q1 FY26.
In Q1 FY27, E&O's property sales more than doubled to RM356.0 million from RM153.0 million in the previous corresponding quarter, reflecting sustained demand for the group's ongoing developments.
Supported by stronger sales momentum, the group's unbilled sales increased 28.4 per cent year-on-year to RM1.7 billion as at June 30, 2026.
The unbilled sales will be recognised over the next few financial years as construction progresses, providing the group with healthy earnings visibility.
Managing director Kok Tuck Cheong said the group experienced encouraging sales take-up from its Penang and Klang Valley property offerings in Q1.
"Beyond our ongoing development activities, we have entered into a joint venture with Cengild Medical Bhd and Skyspring Sdn Bhd to develop a multidisciplinary tertiary private hospital at Andaman Island.
"This partnership represents another important step in transforming Andaman Island into a sustainable waterfront township, while enhancing its appeal to residents and supporting Penang's growing medical tourism sector," he said in a statement.
Kok said the group had also formed a strategic partnership to buy a prime freehold site along Jalan Kia Peng here for a proposed premium high-rise residential development.
He added that the acquisition would further expand the group's development footprint in the Klang Valley and strengthen its premium residential portfolio in one of Kuala Lumpur's most established and desirable locations.
Kok said the group has two upcoming launches for FY27, comprising a waterfront serviced apartment development and landed homes.
"We will be launching these developments towards the end of the financial year," he noted.

Title: Madrasah instructor charged with sexually assaulting two young brothers
Article:
MUAR: A madrasah instructor was charged in the Sessions Court here today with four counts of sexually assaulting two brothers, aged 10 and 11, at a madrasah hostel in Batu Pahat last month.
Muhammad Hilmi Mohamad Noor, 24, pleaded not guilty to all charges before Sessions Court judge Emelia Kaswati Mohamad Khalid.
The accused allegedly committed the offences against the two boys at 4pm in July.
He was charged under Sections 14(a) and 14(b) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.
Section 14 provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction, while Section 16 provides for an additional term of up to five years' imprisonment and at least two strokes of the rotan.
Deputy public prosecutor Amirah Sapian appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
The prosecution proposed bail of RM20,000 for each charge with additional conditions.
However, the court granted bail of RM15,000 for all four charges.
The court also ordered the accused to report monthly to the nearest police station and barred him from approaching or contacting prosecution witnesses, including the victims.
The court set Sept 14 for mention for document submission and the appointment of counsel.

Title: 'Gapai' brings Merdeka spirit to life through generations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The spirit of Merdeka comes to life in "Gapai", a three-minute film launched by Permodalan Nasional Bhd's Merdeka Ventures today.
Inspired by the iconic raised hand of Malaysia's first prime minister, Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj, during the 1957 proclamation of independence, the film follows the lives and experiences of Malaysians across generations.
PNB Merdeka Ventures chief executive officer Datuk Dr Izwan Hasli Mohd Ibrahim said the film also reflected the history and community surrounding the Merdeka 118 precinct, which stands on the site where independence was declared.
"As the custodian of the nation's most significant heritage, we have a responsibility not only to preserve our history, but to ensure it continues to inspire future generations.
"The Merdeka 118 precinct stands on the very ground where Malaysia's independence was declared, and we want every visit here to be a reminder of where we came from and how far we have come," he said at a media luncheon today.
Izwan said "Gapai" featured stories of people from different generations while highlighting the history and community that shaped the area.
He said the film aimed to inspire present and future generations to develop a stronger sense of patriotism and draw inspiration from the nation's journey.
Meanwhile, as part of its Merdeka month celebrations, the Merdeka 118 precinct is collaborating with Locco to host a three-day celebration from Aug 29 to 31 at Stadium Merdeka and Merdeka Boulevard.
The programme will feature a Merdeka Community Bazaar, cultural and heritage activities, a Merdeka flashmob and the WarisanKL Explorace.

Title: #NSTViral: Rohingya family making a 'home' of public spaces in Larkin
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A six-member Rohingya family has been living rough at various public places in Larkin here for more than two months.
A resident in the area said the family had moved between several locations, including a playground, shop lot pavements and the vicinity of a surau.
"They move from one place to another, and I was told this was to avoid action by the authorities.
"Imagine our children wanting to play at the playground, but there are people living there," he said.
The resident urged the authorities to locate the family and take appropriate action.
Larkin assemblyman Mohd Hairi Mad Shah said they were monitoring the situation following complaints from residents.
"Based on the complaints, Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) enforcement officers and police were deployed to the playground.
"They were no longer there this morning," he said when contacted.
Pictures and videos purportedly showing the family staying at a children's playground in Larkin have since gone viral on social media.
Residents claimed in the comments that the playground was along Jalan Sentosa, Kampung Dato' Onn, and that the family had been sleeping there for several nights.
One of the videos also purportedly showed a family member naked.
